title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: Building on the adoption of the Recruitment License and Code of Conduct Rules 2019 and Policy Guidelines for Mandatory Insurance for the Migrant Workers in 2018-2019, the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) adopted one new legal and policy framework the ‘Recruiting Agents Classification Rule 2020' in January 2020. In addition, the revision of the Overseas Employment and Migrant Act (OEMA) 2013 has been formulated and finalised and will be submitted to the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law and Parliamentary. The revised Act closes gaps in legislation that leads to exploitation of migrant workers, particularly in bringing the middlemen into an accountability framework. This revision is done in accordance with the general principles and operational guidelines for fair recruitment. The Ministry of Expatriate Welfare and Overseas Employment (MoEWOE) developed a strategy paper called: "Post-Pandemic Strategic Roadmap for the Labour Migration Sector" along with a need assessment survey from the returnees during COVID period in 2020. The document mapped the vulnerabilities of returned migrant workers during COVID, and proposed a response framework in the form of a reintegration roadmap with an agenda for actions disaggregated over the immediate, midterm and long-term. In March 2021, the MoEWOE launched the Labour Attaches Reporting System. The monthly and annual reporting formats of labour attaches have been completed and officially launched by Minister, Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment. With support of the Government of Switzerland, ILO conducted evidence based researches for government to take new policy directives: 1. Formulation and finalization of Recruiting Agents Classification Rule 2020. 2. Formulation and finalisation of the revision of Overseas Employment and Migrant Act (OEMA) 2013. 3. Technical assistance to develop a Position Paper supporting the Ministry of Expatriate Welfare and Overseas Employment (MoEWOE) to mainstream migration in the National 8th Five Year Plan, and the Perspective Plan of Bangladesh 2021-2041 4. Technical assistance to implement the ‘Cost of Migration National Survey 2020' which is conducted by Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS). 5. Technical assistance to support the MoEWOE to identify specific policy interventions to reduce the migration cost based upon the Cost of Migration Survey findings. 6. Formulation and finalisation of the "Post-Pandemic Strategic Roadmap for the Labour Migration Sector" along with a need assessment survey from the returnees during COVID period in 2020. 7. ILO provided support to its partner Integrated Community & Industrial Development Initiative in Bangladesh (INCIDIN) to prepare discussion paper which is based on a critical review of Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) and Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL)'s current foreign employment practices of women workers for overseas employment, and also based on community based dialogue with informal recruiting agents. ILO, with support of the Government of Switzerland, provided technical support to develop the system, develop the user manual, develop the training materials and train the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training, the Labour Attaches, and the MoEWOE officials.

title.narrative: 7.5.1. Number of member States with labour migration frameworks or institutional mechanisms to protect the labour rights of migrant workers and promote coherence with employment, skills, social protection, and other relevant policies
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: During the reporting period, the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) launched two new or improved services for migrant workers: (1) RAIMS: The development of the ‘Recruitment Agency Information Management System' (RAIMS) was completed and officially launched by Minister, Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment. It represents an information management system where in one click the Ministry can see who are all recruitment agencies registered in Bangladesh, the ones suspended and cancelled. Recruitment Agencies are classified according to their compliance with indicators mentioned in the classification rules, and licences will be suspended if compliance is poor. (2) The ‘Integrated Online Complaint Mechanism System' has been updated to include Mobile APPs and officially launched by Minister, Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment (MoEWOE). Migrant workers fill their complains online, and can follow up progress of their file through online access, while information is being forwarded to MoEWOE for case management and support. The Bangladesh Employers Federation (BEF) developed and disseminated the Business and Financial Management modules for the returnee migrant workers. The modules help returnee migrants in approaching employers, or start a business. 23 participants received a training of trainers. In March 2021, they will further train the potential returnee migrants in their community. With support of the Government of Switzerland, ILO supported the Government of Bangladesh in the following areas: RAIMS: The revised application development of the ‘Recruitment Agency Information Management System' (RAIMS) undertook several adjustments in order to be finalised. Training-of-Trainers (ToT) for end users, i.e. officials from the MoEWOE, BMET, Wedge Earners Welfare Board (WEWB), BOESL and BAIRA, took place in November 2020. Online ‘Complaint Mechanism': The ‘Integrated Online Complaint Mechanism System' has been updated to include Mobile APPs, a web application with database backup, and a testing manual along with a sustainability document. A Training-of-Trainers (TOT) programme for the concerned BMET officials has been organised in April 2021. Apart from the comprehensive web-based Complaint System, the ILO developed a mobile app which can be downloaded from the ‘play store' (Probashi Ovijog). With support of Government of the United Kingdom, ILO provided supported the Bangladesh Employers' Federation to conduct the training. This module was distributed to different Chambers of Commerce and service providers for further training for returnees who are willing to start business.

title.narrative: 7.5.2. Number of countries with new or improved services to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output A.1. More accurate and sustainable statistics on decent work using the latest statistical standards

description.narrative: During the reporting period, the Government of Bangladesh published the ‘Cost of Migration National Survey 2020'. The field work was conducted by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS). The report is uploaded into the Government website The Cost of Migration Survey Report disaggregates recruitment costs across gender, age groups, education levels, countries of destination and skills acquired. It captures and provides insight into the real costs faced monthly by overseas labour migrants. In terms of regular employment earnings, the average recruitment costs for males are 17.6 months of employment, and approximately 5.6 months for female domestic workers. The MoEWOE has requested the ILO to support the Ministry to identify specific policy interventions to reduce the cost based upon the Cost of Migration Survey findings. In addition, during the reporting period series of dissemination workshop took place among GoB officials, social partners, civil society, and private sector. ILO supported the Government of Bangladesh in the following areas in the year of 2020 and 2021. These are: Between September-December 2019, with the support of the ILO, BBS developed and validated its sampling methodology. In addition, pre-testing of Computer Questionnaire (CAPI) were completed in early 2020. Finally, a training of Supervising Officers and Data Collectors was organised in spring 2020 ahead of data collection from approximately 12,000 individual migrant workers.
